title: You Borrow $10,000. Where Does the Money Come From?
sources: McLeay, Radia & Thomas (2014), 'Money creation in the modern economy', Bank of England Quarterly Bulletin 2014 Q1
Federal Reserve Board, Reserve Requirements (ratios set to 0% effective March 26, 2020)

beats.text: Dave wants a car. But Dave has... zero dollars.
So Dave goes to the bank, and asks: can I borrow ten thousand dollars?
Most people think the bank opens a giant safe, full of other people's money, and gives some to Dave.
The bank just types ten thousand into Dave's account. Click. Done.
That money did not exist five seconds ago.
It's like writing: one duck, on a piece of paper. And poof! A brand new duck appears.
But the bank also writes a second paper: Dave owes us ten thousand dollars.
New money for Dave. New debt for Dave. At the same time.
And no, this is not a conspiracy theory. The Bank of England explained it, in twenty fourteen.
Now Dave has to pay it back, with real work, for five years. Plus interest.
So next time a bank smiles and says, we'd love to lend you money... now you know why.
